recommendation: Use per-machine logical frontiers and conservative safe horizons, initially synchronized safe epochs. Keep exact event timestamps as the default; optimize independent horizons only after qualification.

parameters.latency_qualification: Declared benchmark topology parameter, not a proven efficient stop quantum or a guarantee for other effect paths.

assumptions: One caller OS thread owns all machines, devices, scenarios and scheduling decisions.
The backend exposes every cross-machine effect and admits the required stopped-guest coordinates.
Per-machine branch-to-model-nanosecond conversion is pinned, monotonic and qualified for the supported workload profile.
Every possible effect path has a sound production-time and minimum-latency bound; network latency does not bound controller or shared-resource effects.
Blocked wake bounds account for unknown incoming traffic and autonomous kernel/device work; an empty queue alone is insufficient.

definitions.f_i: Committed local world-nanosecond frontier of participant i.
definitions.P_j: Proven earliest timestamp of another unregistered effect from producer j. Use its frontier while runnable; lift it only with a sound blocked/wake/output bound.
definitions.L_ji: Guaranteed minimum effect latency on path j to i, including non-network paths.
definitions.D_i: Next known timer, fault, device, input or assumption-invalidating barrier affecting i.

causal_horizon.rule: Guest work is permitted strictly before H_i. Close possible equal-time arrivals, dispatch events in deadline/registration order, and give ready controllers their turn before guest continuations at the endpoint.
causal_horizon.argument: Known affecting effects occur no earlier than D_i; every unregistered effect occurs no earlier than P_j + L_ji. Thus work strictly before their minimum cannot observe an effect that should already have arrived.
causal_horizon.initial_execution_policy: Use synchronized safe epochs first. Natural exits and newly published deadlines recompute bounds; shared resources and immediate control effects remain coordination points.
causal_horizon.clock_accounting: Do not sum machine elapsed times into world elapsed time. Store per-machine epochs, count/time anchors, rational rates, fractional remainders and blocked-time anchoring; advance a world causal commit frontier only after closure.

counterexamples.name: unknown_peer_send
counterexamples.failure: The receiver has passed the arrival; publishing the packet later cannot repair committed reads or acknowledgments.

counterexamples.name: immediate_controller_effect
counterexamples.failure: A reliable crash/heal/inspection command bypasses network latency and arrives behind the workload frontier.
counterexamples.required_rule: Timestamp commands by controller-local issue time, queue them, close the affected-machine barrier, then apply and acknowledge them. Host receipt order and a global dispatch cursor are not their simulated issue time.

counterexamples.name: direct_shared_state
counterexamples.failure: Shared memory, shared-disk arbitration or direct cross-machine DMA bypasses the link bound.
counterexamples.required_rule: Represent a separate effect path, possibly with zero lookahead, and coordinate it. Process sharing inside one VM remains local.

counterexamples.name: fault_evaluation_moved_to_batch_endpoint
counterexamples.failure: Evaluating all packets against endpoint fault state delivers a packet that should have been dropped at its original timestamp.

controller_and_topology.runnable_controller: Immediate possible commands bound affected workload horizons by the controller frontier. Run the controller to a known blocked continuation or coordinate a barrier.
controller_and_topology.command_timestamps: Control commands are timestamped effects even though their transport is reliable and outside the faultable fabric.
controller_and_topology.changes: A known heal or policy change that reduces a bound is a barrier before affected progress. Invalidate/recompute horizon certificates and explicitly define in-flight rescheduling; never backdate delivery.
controller_and_topology.zero_latency: Zero-latency network/direct-resource cycles provide no positive lookahead. Use coordinated event/microstep ordering or declare them outside the coarse-epoch profile.

quantities.beta_i: Measured guest-branch throughput in branches per host second.
quantities.C_i: Measured host seconds for stop, correction, completed-I/O, witness and control overhead.

performance.admission: Invert the local time mapping without upward rounding to find an admitted count/RIP/REP target at or before the safe bound. Rate calibration does not manufacture exact stopping or progress on zero-count paths.
performance.conflict_rule: If an affordable quantum cannot fit the safe horizon, preserve exact deadlines and report the O5 conflict. Change qualified costs/profile/architecture rather than silently extending the horizon.
performance.calibration_inputs: Freeze calibration and performance policy inputs. Current-run host elapsed time, administrative retries or load must not change canonical scheduling or virtual clocks.

safe: A host loop may process original timestamped transitions in deadline/registration order.
After each callback, resume a ready controller before the next equal-time event.
Break the batch when guest execution or another newly runnable participant is required before the next timestamp.
Amortize bookkeeping or commuting bulk work only when no intervening observation, dependency or intervention is possible.
rejected: Drain an entire timestamp before its awakened controller.
Move all logical delivery times to an epoch endpoint.
Evaluate earlier delivery-time faults using later healed state.
Advance past known deadlines and repair timestamps afterward.
batching.lateness_profile: Bounded lateness is a distinct later profile with an explicit tested bound and scheduled/dispatched/IRQ-ready/injected timestamps. Exact fabric/device arrival and later legal IRQ handling are distinct observations; exact dispatch rejects overruns.

seeded_scheduling.bounds: Seeded cuts and timer/readiness variations stay within admitted causal horizons and the declared legal delivery profile.
seeded_scheduling.linux_threads: A host KVM stop alone does not switch Linux threads. Guest timer/IRQ or readiness changes must reach Linux scheduling with meaningful runnable alternatives.
seeded_scheduling.required_sensitivity: Observe actual guest task-switch/order or application shared-state changes, not merely different host-stop labels.
seeded_scheduling.administration: Debug/completion retries consume no canonical RNG, time or boundary number.

api_delta.change: Per-participant ClockState plus world commit time

api_delta.invariant: Reject stale certificates and actual progress beyond their bound.
Reject retroactive effects; direct control effects require affected-machine barrier admission before application/acknowledgment.

api_delta.change: Ordered dispatch and explicit delivery profile

retained_source_gaps.gap: Successive branch deltas currently advance one scalar clock; replace this for the real multi-machine exact profile.
max(now, due) dispatch is not a qualified exact-production lateness rule; replace it with explicit deadline/overrun handling.

not_shown: measured per-machine calibration or stop costs
